source_text: Et haec quidem dixerim, ut statim appareret, te esse aut imperitiae aut impudentiae singularis, qui tuorum vice, contrariis utereris; ceterum pietas explanabit et ratio, Deum meum neminem in contumeliam formare.
pass_a_gloss: And these things indeed I would have said, that it would appear at once, that you are of either unskillfulness or shamelessness singular, who in the place of your own, would use contraries; for the rest piety will explain and reason, that my God forms no one unto insult.
pass_b_english: I have said this to make it immediately apparent that you possess extraordinary ignorance or shamelessness, using statements opposed to you as though they were your own. Piety and reason, however, will explain that my God forms no one for dishonor,

choices.why: Julian's ethical charge: habit of sinning kills pudor.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
